discovery: Establishing neutron-star mergers as sites of r-process nucleosynthesis: prediction and modelling of kilonovae powered by the radioactive decay of freshly synthesized heavy nuclei
motivation: Where the elements heavier than iron were made was one of the great open questions of physics. Lattimer (with the late Schramm) first proposed that neutron-rich matter ejected in compact-object mergers undergoes rapid neutron capture. Metzger and collaborators showed that the radioactive decay of these r-process nuclei must power a distinctive transient, the kilonova, and predicted its luminosity and timescale. Kasen and collaborators calculated the extreme lanthanide opacities that make kilonovae red and long-lived. These predictions were confirmed in detail by the optical and infrared counterpart of GW170817, turning the r-process site from speculation into a quantitative, testable problem. The work links laboratory nuclear physics, masses, half-lives and fission of exotic nuclei, directly to observed light curves and spectra, and it now guides measurement programmes at radioactive-beam facilities worldwide.
